subject: ingles
statement:
Lee el texto original de práctica:
“Library notice: The reading room opens at nine. Bring your student card to borrow a book. Each visitor may borrow two books for seven days. Food is not allowed in the reading room, but sealed water bottles are permitted.”

What must a visitor bring to borrow a book?
explanation:
1. La evidencia pertinente es: “Bring your student card to borrow a book.”.
2. La tarjeta se menciona como requisito para el préstamo.
3. La respuesta respaldada por el texto es: A student card.

“Library notice: The reading room opens at nine. Bring your student card to borrow a book. Each visitor may borrow two books for seven days. Food is not allowed in the reading room, but sealed water bottles are permitted.”

What does but signal in the last sentence?
options: A contrast between a restriction and an exception.
A causal explanation of the opening time.
explanation:
1. La evidencia pertinente es: “Food is not allowed in the reading room, but sealed water bottles are permitted.”.
2. But conecta dos disposiciones contrastantes; no indica una fecha ni una causa.
3. La respuesta respaldada por el texto es: A contrast between a restriction and an exception.

subject: ingles
statement:
Lee el texto original de práctica:
“The school garden opened in April. Students water it on Tuesdays and Thursdays. A teacher checks the soil before they add water. The project aims to help students learn about plants, not to sell vegetables.”

Which activity is not a stated goal of the garden project?
explanation:
1. La evidencia pertinente es: “not to sell vegetables”.
2. La negación afecta explícitamente al objetivo de vender verduras.
3. La respuesta respaldada por el texto es: Selling vegetables.

2. Los estudiantes son quienes riegan; el pronombre retoma ese sujeto plural.
3. La respuesta respaldada por el texto es: The students.

subject: ingles
statement:
Lee el texto original de práctica:
“Nina studies in the morning. On Fridays she works at a library from two to five. The library is closed on Sundays. She walks there because it is near her home.”

Can we conclude that Nina never uses any transport other than walking?
options: No; the text says she always drives.
No; the text only states how she gets to the library.
Yes; it describes every journey she takes.
Yes; she lives inside the library.
explanation:
1. La evidencia pertinente es: “She walks there because it is near her home.”.
2. La información sobre ese trayecto no justifica una afirmación universal sobre todos sus viajes.
3. La respuesta respaldada por el texto es: No; the text only states how she gets to the library.

subject: ingles
statement:
Lee el texto original de práctica:
“Library notice: The reading room opens at nine. Bring your student card to borrow a book. Each visitor may borrow two books for seven days. Food is not allowed in the reading room, but sealed water bottles are permitted.”

Which summary is best supported?
options: Visitors must borrow exactly seven books.
The room opens only on Sundays.
The notice explains access, borrowing limits and reading-room rules.
explanation:
1. La evidencia pertinente es: “Bring your student card to borrow a book. Each visitor may borrow two books for seven days.”.
2. El resumen reúne los asuntos tratados sin alterar cantidades ni añadir días no indicados.
3. La respuesta respaldada por el texto es: The notice explains access, borrowing limits and reading-room rules.
